s: A company spends $180,000 per month on Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances across three AWS Regions, and usage is steady. Over the next 12 months, the company plans to move most workloads from x86-based M5 and C5 instances to Graviton-based instances, move several services to AWS Fargate, and possibly move one workload to a different Region. The company is willing to commit to a 3-year term. Which purchase option provides a significant discount while continuing to cover the usage after these changes?
o: Purchase 3-year EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the M5 and C5 families in each Region.
Purchase 3-year Compute Savings Plans sized to the steady hourly compute spend.
Purchase 3-year Standard Reserved Instances with regional scope for the current instance types.
Purchase 3-year Convertible Reserved Instances and exchange them as workloads move to Graviton-based instances.

w.y: Compute Savings Plans apply automatically to EC2 usage regardless of instance family, size, operating system or Region, and also to Fargate and Lambda. They continue to cover the usage after moves to Graviton, Fargate and another Region, while still giving up to 66% savings.

o.A: Locked to an instance family in a Region; Graviton families, Fargate and the Region move would fall outside coverage.
o.B: Correct: flexible across family, Region, EC2, Fargate and Lambda.
o.C: Cannot change instance family and do not apply to Fargate.
o.D: Exchanges are manual, RIs stay in one Region and never cover Fargate usage.

d: continuing to cover the usage after these changes
